eclass/arc-build: Make library dependencies available from target sysroot Currently prebuilt Android libraries, including their pkgconfig files and the pkg-config wrapper itself are located outside of the target sysroot. This poses a problem when using localy built libraries as dependencies of other packages is desired. This patch adds arc-build and arc-build-nyc ebuilds that install pkgconfig files, pkg-config wrapper and a symlink to the prebuilt binaries to /opt/google/containers/android, so that all the build prerequisites are available within the target sysroot. install_toolchain: do not die if ${toolchain}/go is not installed. Having go installed as part of a toolchain was always optional. install_toolchain_in_provided() function has a check if $go_ver is empty, and only adds go to package.provided if it's not. Unfortunately, cross_get_version() was dying if go is not found. I've split cross_get_version() into two functions. The original cross_get_version() does not die if the package is not found. A new function cross_get_version_or_die() checks the results and dies if the package was not found. Checking go version uses cross_get_version(). Checking gcc/glibc version uses cross_get_version_or_die(). BUG=None TEST='setup_board --board=x86-zgb' works after disabling i686-pc-linux-gnu-go in cl/444042. CRAS: system_state - Store target capture gain System capture gain is subjected to supported gain range. This causes a problem that when desired capture gain is out of supported gain range, it can not be retained after supported gain range is changed because the information is lost. To solve above problem, system state can add a field capture_gain_target to store the desired capture gain. Then, when the supported range is changed, system state can try to re-apply capture_gain_target. Initalize device setting in alsa_iodev_set_active_node so the gain limit and system gain can be adjusted based on the latest active device and active node. BUG=chrome-os-partner:60744, chromium:692187 TEST=make check TEST=on kevin, check cras_test_client --dump_s and see default system gain is 20.0 dB, not 0.0dB. TEST=Use apprtc, switch between internal mic and external mic and see the gain adjusted on one node is retained after switching back to that node.
